prerequisites: Previous knowledge, skills, and attitudes, specifically those from Graphic Expression I.

learning_outcomes.text: Use Technical Drawing as a communication language in terms of both work methodologies and tools used.
Apply the concept of Standardization: presentation formats, scales, symbology, etc., in graphical representations.
Solve geometric problems and apply them in the construction of industrial parts.
Interpret technical drawings and assembly plans, distinguishing between the functions of each element.
Represent common industrial elements (threads, keys, gears, bearings, welding, etc.), know their designation and standardization.
Consult regulations, analyzing and structuring information.
Analyze and compare the characteristics and applications of the most used CAD programs in Engineering.
Know and manage a CAD program, using all its possibilities for entity definition, geometric transformations, drawing aids, dimensioning, etc., transferring previously acquired concepts and skills.
Get started with CAE and parametric design tools.
Manage a project-based CAD system.
Locate, analyze, and structure necessary information for projects.
Integrate drawings with other applications to generate comprehensible and organized technical documentation.
Work in a team, assuming responsibility and collaborating with colleagues.
Plan activities to deliver work within assigned times and with required quality.
Participate in class with respect and argue with rational criteria.
Knows and symbolically represents the surface condition of mechanical assemblies and parts.
Represents conical and inclined surfaces and dimensions them according to standards.
Analyzes and represents different types of joints and their standardized elements.
Knows and represents standardized mechanical elements: Gears, bearings, springs, etc.
Creates 3D solids with boolean operations and their development.

syllabus_topics: Drawing plans: assembly and detail drawings.
Generation using CAE tools: Work with solids.
Drawing and interpretation of axonometric views.
Topic 0: EGI content relevant for EGII. Inventor 2021 tutorials.
teaching_methods: Expository class: Participatory lecture, conferences, company visits, attendance at fairs, etc.
Participatory class: Individual or group. Case resolution, role-playing, technical application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.
Laboratory/computer practice: Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Integrated project: Carrying out a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.
Tutoring: Carrying out a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.
Group work: Individual and group preparation of essays, problem-solving, projects, etc. For submission and presentation in practical classes.
Individual work: Student study: preparation of readings, exam preparation, exercise elaboration, class preparation, etc.
assessment_rules: Evaluation is continuous and personalized. For written tests, a score of 4 or higher is required for the grade to be averaged. To pass the course, in both first and second calls, an average grade of 5 or higher is required. Students have 2 annual calls per course to pass written tests, and can recover academic assignment grades in the second call by completing alternative exercises. For late submissions, points will be deducted proportionally to the delay, up to a maximum of 5 points; after one week, the assignment will receive a grade of 0. If an assignment grade is below 5, the student can resubmit it for a maximum grade of 5. For students exempt from the integrated project, its 25% weight will be distributed equally among the other assessment instruments.
